title: Kopo Kopo's Turn From Microlenders to Nairobi's Small Shops
conflicts: How few merchants could take M-Pesa: Higgins (PandoDaily 2013) said Safaricom had about 100 formal merchant accounts; Lyon (Business Daily 2014) said only three chains were on its buy-goods service; GSMA (2014) gives Kopo Kopo's 2011 estimate of under 0.01% of businesses. The story gives GSMA's figure and Higgins's 100, attributed. Early funding: $725,000 seed from Khosla Impact (PandoDaily) vs $1 million previous venture funding (PYMNTS); the story names the October 2011 investors (VC4A) without an amount. Origin: founders' Sierra Leone/Seattle account (VC4A, PYMNTS 2011) vs Business Daily's US-market version; founders' account used.
notes: Arc changed from the slate's founding-decision to change-of-direction: the documented episode is the pivot from a non-profit microcredit tool in Sierra Leone to a for-profit merchant-payments service in Kenya. Ben Lyon is named as co-founder alongside Higgins; third co-founder Tom Bostlemann stayed in the US and is mentioned only in research_notes. PandoDaily article is cited from a copy on a Pace University course page. GSMA PDF loads but the verifier does not find the company name in it, so it is supplementary.
